content:
Apple TV has today announced that two highly anticipated new series are in the works. One is a comedy starring heavyweight names, and the other is adapted from a brand-new romance novel by a popular author.

First: "Protective Custody" is a brand-new comedy starring Benicio Del Toro and Ben Stiller.

Ben Stiller has deep ties with Apple TV. Aside from playing a small role in "The Dink" released this week, he usually works behind the scenes.

However, Apple has announced a brand-new comedy series "Protective Custody," which brings Stiller from behind the scenes to in front of the camera, co-starring with another superstar Benicio Del Toro. News of the series was announced through a post on X:

Show creators Judge, Hely and King have rich comedy experience, having respectively worked on "King of the Hill," "Veep" and "Parks and Recreation."

The story tells of a "disgraced financier" living his new life under protective custody while awaiting trial after being arrested.

Second: "Peculiar Stars" is a brand-new romance series by popular "Fourth Wing" author Rebecca Yarros.

Comedy, sci-fi and thriller are Apple's main genres, while romance is an area this streaming platform has somewhat neglected. However, a new series announced today may start to change that situation.

"Peculiar Stars" is Rebecca Yarros's new work—she is the author of the wildly popular romantic fantasy "Fourth Wing" series. The book will be published this November (pre-order now), and Apple has just secured the adaptation rights to turn it into a TV series.

The news was announced by Apple TV's X account. Although the official announcement did not specify, according to Deadline, the plan is to adapt "Peculiar Stars" into a TV series, not a film.

Here is the story synopsis obtained through Deadline:

Neither project has announced a release date yet—they are expected to be 2027 releases, or possibly even later.

In the nearer future, Apple will celebrate the highly anticipated return of "Ted Lasso" in a few weeks. Currently, the third season of "Silo" is airing to rave reviews, and a new season of sci-fi series "Dark Matter" is also about to return.

Apple TV costs US$12.99 per month, and can also be subscribed at a discounted price through the Apple One bundle.
